headline_marked: [[Tesla's SI6 chip promises 80X compute]] over current HW4, unveils new 'Super Intelligence' branding
headline: Tesla's SI6 chip promises 80X compute over current HW4, unveils new 'Super Intelligence' branding
summary: The company's revamped AI accelerator roadmap details the SI6 inference chip's massive performance leap and the D3 training chip's shift to a multi-chiplet design with stacked HBM for increased memory capacity.
details: Tesla has unveiled its updated AI accelerator roadmap, introducing the 'Super Intelligence' (SI) branding for its chips, replacing 'AI'. The upcoming 6th Generation inference accelerator, SI6, is projected to deliver an 80x increase in compute performance compared to the existing 4th Generation chip, HW4.

The roadmap also details the D3 training accelerator, which will move away from an SRAM-centric architecture. Instead, it will adopt a multi-chiplet design featuring stacked HBM, a significant departure from previous designs like the Dojo D1's system-on-wafer architecture.

This shift to HBM suggests Tesla's intention to substantially boost memory capacity, crucial for modern AI models that demand extensive memory for parameters and data. While HBM simplifies memory scaling, it introduces new trade-offs in latency, bandwidth, packaging, and power consumption.

Tesla describes the Dojo D3 as optimized for 'space, training, and scaling,' implying high performance and ease of integration. Intriguingly, it is also set to be optimized for extraterrestrial deployments, potentially indicating radiation hardening for specific versions.

The SI6 inference accelerator is estimated to achieve between 17.28 and 46.08 POPS (quadrillion operations per second), depending on how HW4 performance is measured. It is also expected to offer 9x more memory than HW4, marking a substantial upgrade.

The roadmap also confirms the re-emergence of the in-house developed Dojo training accelerator. This comes after Elon Musk had previously canceled the wafer-level Dojo project and stated that SpaceX and xAI would exclusively use Nvidia hardware.

headline_marked: [[Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck]] next year to focus on robotaxis
headline: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year to focus on robotaxis
summary: CEO Elon Musk announced the move on X, citing plans to reallocate factory space to produce more Cybercab robotaxis after years of underwhelming Cybertruck sales.
details: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced on X that the company will stop making the Cybertruck next year. The factory space currently used for the electric pickup will be reallocated to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis.

This decision follows just a few years of underwhelming sales for the futuristic, steel-clad EV. Musk had predicted sales of around 250,000 per year, but Tesla has sold only tens of thousands in total since its late 2023 launch.

The move aligns with Tesla's broader strategy to become an AI- and robotics-focused company, with robotaxi ambitions at its core. The company has been testing Cybercabs in Austin, Texas, and plans to expand operations to Dallas.
This is the third product Tesla has discontinued to fuel these ambitions. Earlier this year, Model S and Model X production ended to free up factory space for Optimus humanoid robots.

First announced in 2019, the Cybertruck was a long-time obsession for Musk, who promised an "amazing pickup truck" inspired by cyberpunk sci-fi designs like Blade Runner. Its radical design certainly stood out.

However, the company overpromised on basic specs from the start. At its infamous 2019 reveal, Tesla claimed a starting price under $40,000 and up to 500 miles of range, neither of which were achieved.

After a two-year delay, partly due to the pandemic, the truck launched in late 2023 with a base price inflated to around $60,000 and top-end range reduced by over 100 miles. Musk described it as "the finest in apocalyptic equipment."

The truck has struggled on the market due to its polarizing design and higher-than-expected price. Political factors, including Musk's financial backing of Donald Trump, also turned the recognizable vehicle into a target for protesters.
